articles.title: China has put 2,000 servers in sea near Shanghai, taking off from a Microsoft project that shutdown in 2020, where the company sank 855 servers in North Sea
articles.summary: Tech News News: China has switched on a commercial underwater data centre off the coast of Shanghai, dropping roughly 2,000 servers onto the seabed in the Lingang Spe.
articles.body: China has switched on a commercial underwater data centre off the coast of Shanghai, dropping roughly 2,000 servers onto the seabed in the Lingang Special Area and wiring them directly into an offshore wind farm. The facility runs at 24MW, sits 10 metres below the surface and more than 10km out, and uses the surrounding seawater in place of chillers and cooling towers. It took 1.6 billion yuan of investment, roughly Rs 2,100 crore, and is a joint effort between HiCloud Technology and state-owned China Communications Construction. Commercial operations began in May, after trials in February and construction wrapping up last October.The design it borrows from belongs to Microsoft. In 2018 the company lowered a white steel cylinder the size of a shipping container 117 feet under the North Sea off the Orkney Islands, with 855 servers inside and 27.6 petabytes of storage. The air was pumped out first and replaced with dry nitrogen, so nothing inside could oxidise or take on moisture. Two years later Microsoft pulled it back up, published results better than anyone expected, and then walked away from the idea entirely.Microsoft's underwater servers failed at one-eighth the rate of its land serversThe number that made the experiment famous was the failure rate. Microsoft lost six of the 855 servers on the seabed. A control group running identical jobs in an ordinary building on land lost eight out of 135. That works out to 0.7% underwater against 5.9% on land. Two things explain it. Cold seawater carried heat away at no cost, and a sealed tube filled with nitrogen and off limits to humans removed slow corrosion and the accidental knocks that wear down land hardware over years. Power usage effectiveness came in at 1.07, with no mechanical cooling at all, at a time when most of the industry was still sitting above 1.5.China's underwater data centre runs GPU clusters for AI trainingThe Shanghai pod is not a proof of concept. It carries GPU clusters doing AI training, big data annotation and work on domestic large language models, with computing capacity deployed by China Telecom and local service providers. Its developers put its PUE at around 1.15, claim a 22.8% cut in electricity consumption, no water use at all, and more than 90% less land than an equivalent site onshore. The Chinese government says the project is designed to run on more than 95% green electricity. HiCloud first sank servers off Hainan in 2021 and set up the first commercial modules there in 2023. It has talked about taking the offshore wind model up to 500MW.Seawater cooling cuts the power bill and removes the freshwater bill entirelyThe timing is what makes an old experiment relevant. In a land-based facility, somewhere between a quarter and half of total electricity demand goes to moving chilled water around the servers. Training clusters are pushing density past what ordinary buildings can handle, and grid operators in Virginia and Texas have started resisting new data centre connections. A sealed module offshore avoids both halves of the problem. The sea absorbs the heat, the turbines overhead supply the electricity, and no aquifer gets touched. A United Nations university institute warned this week that the water footprint of data centres could hit 9.3 trillion litres by 2030, roughly what the entire population of sub-Saharan Africa uses domestically in a year.Marine biologists say the warming around the pods stays localThe obvious objection is that a heat source on the seabed is still a heat source. Researchers who study coastal ecosystems say the risks, including disturbed sediment and warmer water immediately around the modules, look manageable but need monitoring over time. Rick Stafford, a marine biologist at Bournemouth University, said cooling with seawater does raise local temperatures but that the effect will "not be far reaching". Microsoft's own cylinder came back up wearing algae, barnacles and anemones grown to the size of melons, which answered a question nobody had asked about whether sea life would mind the hardware.Microsoft shut Project Natick down even though the numbers workedMicrosoft confirmed in 2024 that its subsea programme was over. Noelle Walsh, who runs the company's cloud operations and innovation group, said flatly that she was not building subsea data centres anywhere in the world. The reasoning was practical rather than technical. Sending a technician down in a strong current to fix a failed board is expensive, saltwater still eats steel, and Microsoft has been building on land at a pace it has no reason to slow. A researcher at Hong Kong Polytechnic University put the gap simply: Microsoft got to the concept first, while China had the market demand, marine engineering and policy backing to turn it into a working commercial site. Around 90% of the world's AI data centre capacity now sits in those two countries.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: In 2023, a Texas family donated 100 acres of ranch land to Odessa; 3 years later, a $145 million sports complex with 30 indoor courts and 22 outdoor fields is taking shape
articles.summary: US News: Sometimes, the right gift, at the right time, can turn into something that thousands can benefit from. Just like the 100 acres of land a Texas family .
articles.body: Sometimes, the right gift, at the right time, can turn into something that thousands can benefit from. Just like the 100 acres of land a Texas family gifted to the City of Odessa, which is becoming a $145 million sports and recreation hub. The construction work will hit another major milestone next month, with a topping-out ceremony scheduled for October 7 to mark the progress on the transformational project. The complex will function as both a neighbourhood recreation hub and a tournament destination. The complex includes 30 indoor courts and 22 outdoor fields for leagues and pick-up play. Regionally, the facility has enough capacity to host simultaneous competitions, which means it can draw tournament traffic from across the state. The amphitheatre adds a civic gathering space that serves concerts and community events. The 100-acre ranch land will be part training centre, part competition venue and part community park.A Texas family’s giftIn May 2023, the Bell family in Texas generously donated 100 acres of land at 7777 N. Faudree Road, around the intersection of North Faudree Road and Yukon Road. Their gift came along with a vision. The family wanted the residents of Odessa to have something the area didn't have before: a beautiful space for sports and community gathering. In January 2026, the project had moved from concept to construction. City leaders, the Bell family and community partners came together for the official groundbreaking and kickoff of the $145 million Odessa Sports Complex and Amy Bell Memorial Park. Ellen and Larry Bell, who led the initiative, later pledged an additional $3.6 million towards the Amy Bell Memorial Children's Park section, called ‘Amy’s Park’, expanding the project's reach further to younger residents. What started as a family's decision to donate ranch land has become a significant municipal investment and also a haven for residents.The topping-out ceremony on October 7The topping-out ceremony scheduled for October 7 marks an important milestone in the construction, as the steel structure reaches its full height. With the foundation and main structural work largely complete, construction will move to the next phase. The ceremony will also recognise the progress made and the team’s efforts to keep the large-scale project on schedule and within budget.Putting together 100 acres of land into a functional sports complex requires precision. The city partnered with Sports Facilities Companies to design the layout. Paul Stresing Associates handled the design work. Lee Lewis Construction manages the build. Sports Med Properties brought expertise in how courts and fields should be engineered for different sports. The upcoming event will provide an opportunity to recognise and appreciate this team effort. “The City of Odessa looks forward to celebrating this important construction milestone as work continues on a facility that will become an important part of Odessa’s future,” the officials said in a release.Whether the complex draws the anticipated tournament traffic and serves the community as intended will depend partly on execution over the next year. For now, October 7 marks the moment when that vision moves from blueprint to steel and concrete. The topping-out in October 2026 means crews have completed major structural work. Interior finishes, court installation and systems testing follow. The facility is likely 12–18 months away from opening day.What the complex has to offerThe Odessa Sports Complex at 7777 N. Faudree Road (Yukon Road and Faudree Road area) will be a game-changer for Texas residents. A facility of this size typically serves two populations: locals who use it regularly for recreation and leagues, and visitors who travel to tournaments. The indoor facilities of the complex include 10 basketball courts, 20 volleyball courts and several pickleball courts, along with dedicated fitness and training areas. The outdoor amenities include 10 rectangular fields for soccer and football. There are 12 other diamond fields for baseball and softball. Along with that, a community amphitheatre will be set up for events and performances. Odessa's youth can now train and compete without travelling hours for competitions. All of these facilities will draw teams from several states. This also means more hotel stays, restaurant traffic and promising economic growth for the area.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: An Indian-origin healthcare worker has died after being struck by a semi-trailer near Canberra, Australia, just three weeks after the birth of his second daughter.Harsh Sharma, 30, was hit on the Federal Highway near Bungendore Road at Bywong, about 25 kilometres northeast of Canberra, at around 9.40 pm on Thursday, September 3. articles.title: 'World expects concrete results': PM Modi extends best wishes as Brics chairship passes to China
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday extended his best wishes to China, which will host the next Brics summit in 2027, saying the world n.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday extended his best wishes to China, which will host the next Brics summit in 2027, saying the world now expects “concrete results” as the grouping entered its third decade.Addressing the open session on the second and final day of the Brics Summit in New Delhi, PM Modi said, “Brics is poised to enter its third decade. The world now expects concrete results from us, not just ideas and commitments. I am confident that through our collective efforts, we will certainly live up to these expectations.”The Prime Minister also thanked the leaders and their teams for making the New Delhi Summit a success and wished China well as the next host of the grouping.“I extend my best wishes once again to China as the next host of Brics. I especially commend all of you and your teams for making the New Delhi Summit a success. I wish you all a pleasant and safe journey,” he said, according to ANI.PM highlights Global South’s growing trustSpeaking at a session on “Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth,” PM Modi said the trust of Global South nations in Brics had grown.He highlighted the grouping’s initiatives on disaster management, cooperation among micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and environmental protection.“India has advanced the spirit of friendship, partnership, and cooperation through the Brics platform,” PM Modi said.“We have endeavoured to ensure that Brics cooperation is not limited to governments alone; we want our entrepreneurs, farmers, researchers, women, youth, and ordinary citizens to become active participants as well,” he added.“I can say from personal experience that the trust of Global South nations in Brics has grown, because their voices are heard, their experiences are respected, and solutions are crafted not just for them, but with them. The strength of Brics lies in our diversity and cooperation. We may be rooted in different realities, but together we rise through cooperation and blossom for humanity. May our diversity remain our identity, our cooperation serve as our inspiration, and our progress benefit all of humanity,” he noted.Xi calls for stronger Brics roleChinese President Xi Jinping called for a stronger role for Brics in advancing the interests of the Global South, urging the grouping to “seize the historical initiative” and become an “active, stabilising and positive force in international affairs”.Addressing the second session of the 18th Brics Summit, Xi thanked PM Modi and the Indian government for hosting the two-day summit.According to an official statement released by China’s ministry of foreign affairs, Xi said the Global South had emerged as a “key driver of world multipolarity” and urged Brics countries to work together to advance its interests.“To bring stability to the world and make it a better place, Brics countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, be an active, stabilizing and positive force in international affairs, and advance the well-being of all humanity,” Xi said.Xi called for greater participation of developing countries in global decision-making and stressed the importance of multilateralism.“All countries, regardless of their size, strength or wealth, are equal members of the international community,” he said, urging Global South countries to “hold high the banner of multilateralism” and uphold the authority and role of the United Nations.He also backed reforms to the international financial architecture to increase the “representation and voice of developing countries”. Xi called for greater cooperation through the New Development Bank.On development, Xi said Global South countries should remain committed to the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. “To achieve great things, one should always put the people first,” he added.China proposes five initiativesXi outlined five initiatives to deepen Brics cooperation in artificial intelligence, trade and investment, digital industries, intelligent manufacturing, and science and technology talent development.Under the AI initiative, China proposed establishing a Brics AI open-source community, supporting cooperation in developing and applying large language models, and organising specialised AI seminars and training courses.“First, the open source and inclusive AI initiative. China will be a pioneer in establishing a Brics AI open source community, support cooperation in developing and applying large language models, hold specialized AI seminars and training courses, and build an open ecosystem for AI,” Xi said.On trade and investment, China proposed a Brics special economic zone partnership and announced plans to hold the Brics Forum on Trade in Services next year.“Second, the trade and investment facilitation initiative. China proposes to establish a Brics special economic zone partnership, under which countries can set up an intelligent portal, coordinate policies, and build a new frontier for open development. In an effort to cultivate new drivers of economic and trade cooperation, China will hold the Brics Forum on Trade in Services next year. We welcome your active participation,” he added.China also proposed a Brics digital ecosystem cloud platform and cooperation in digital skills, technology exchange and industrial development.“Third, the digital industry cooperation initiative. China will push for establishing a Brics digital ecosystem cloud platform, and conduct digital skills training, technological exchange and industrial alignment, so as to jointly enable the development of the digital economy,” Xi said.Under the intelligent manufacturing initiative, China offered to assist fellow Brics countries in building smart factories and developing common standards.“Fourth, the intelligent manufacturing cooperation initiative. China stands ready to assist fellow Brics countries in building smart factories and developing standards and norms, and jointly promote manufacturing transformation and upgrading,” he said.Xi also proposed a Brics engineer cultivation alliance and a youth exchange programme for scientific and technological innovation.“Fifth, the science and technology talent development initiative. China proposes to set up a Brics engineer cultivation alliance for joint development of engineers and mutual recognition of competency standards. China will launch a Brics youth exchange program for scientific and technological innovation, so as to cultivate more high-caliber talent,” he said.Xi called for a people-centred approach to emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, and backed the creation of a global AI governance framework based on consensus.He also urged stronger cooperation on climate change and called for the “full and effective implementation of the Paris Agreement”.As India concluded its 2026 Brics chairship, Xi said China would continue to promote high-quality development, high-standard opening up and cooperation with other countries. Xi later departed New Delhi after attending the two-day summit.PM Modi shares summit photographsPM Modi also shared a series of posts and photographs from the summit on X. “Brics Summit related interactions continue at Bharat Mandapam,” he said in one post, sharing photographs with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.He also posted a photograph of Brics leaders at the summit’s family photo event.“With leaders of Brics Member and Partner Countries, Outreach Invitees and Heads of International Organisations together at Brics Summit in New Delhi. A powerful reflection of the growing strength and global resonance of the Brics family. We are connected by a shared vision of cooperation, furthering the spirit of partnership and progress,” he wrote.Earlier, PM Modi welcomed the leaders of Brics member and partner countries, outreach invitees and heads of international organisations at Bharat Mandapam.“Another productive morning at Bharat Mandapam. Happy to welcome the Leaders of Brics Member and Partner Countries, Outreach Invitees and Heads of International Organisations,” he said in another post. China will assume the rotating Brics presidency in 2027 and host the 19th Brics Summit.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Goa First’: AAP, GFP announce alliance for 2027 assembly polls
articles.summary: PANAJI: The AAP and Goa Forward Party (GFP) on Sunday announced their pre-poll alliance, “Goa First”, for the 2027 assembly elections in the coastal s.
articles.body: PANAJI: The AAP and Goa Forward Party (GFP) on Sunday announced their pre-poll alliance, “Goa First”, for the 2027 assembly elections in the coastal state, offering what they described as a non-BJP, non-Congress alternative to voters.Making the announcement, AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal told reporters in Panaji that the ruling BJP would not secure a majority in the upcoming elections and that the ‘Goa First’ alliance would form the next government.He also said that AAP had learnt a lesson after seven of its Rajya Sabha MPs merged with the BJP and would be extra cautious in future about picking candidates.“The people of Goa want a change. Goa First will form the government. We will win on our own,” Kejriwal said at the press conference in the presence of GFP president Vijai Sardesai, Delhi’s leader of opposition and AAP’s Goa desk in-charge Atishi and others.He described the alliance as credible and honest, saying it was loyal to the people of Goa.Kejriwal said both parties were equal partners in the alliance.Sardesai said the tie-up would provide an alternative to a government which, he alleged, was full of defectors.He said the BJP had not received a complete mandate in the previous elections and that even the Congress leadership could not deny the possibility of another round of defections.“It was important to form the alliance. We have formed the alliance with AAP where prioritisation of the interests of Goa is the focus,” Sardesai said.He said the alliance was open to more political forces.“This alliance has not closed the door; it is open to the like-minded political forces. Many people have approached us, including leaders from both the parties who are tired of their politics,” he said.In the current 40-seat Goa legislative assembly, AAP has two MLAs while GFP has one. Sardesai’s party was an alliance partner of Congress in 2022 elections.About the recent movement of their seven Rajya Sabha MPs to the BJP, Kejriwal said they had learnt a lesson and would be “extra cautious” while selecting nominees to the Upper House of Parliament in the future.“It is a matter of great regret that our Rajya Sabha MPs left the party. They betrayed the party. The party sent them to the Rajya Sabha; the people did not send them,” Kejriwal said.He said the AAP had never betrayed the people through its elected representatives.“We believe that this is a lesson for us because such a thing has never happened in the Aam Aadmi Party before. From now onwards, before sending anyone to the Rajya Sabha, we will scrutinise the person thoroughly and ensure that he is the right person,” he said.Kejriwal cited his party’s experience in Delhi, Goa, Jammu and Kashmir and Gujarat to claim that its elected representatives had remained loyal to AAP despite alleged attempts to engineer defections. He said the party has one MLA in J&K and five in Gujarat.He said the people of Goa had elected two AAP MLAs in the 2022 Assembly polls and alleged that attempts had been made to get them to switch sides. “Both our MLAs did not break away,” he said.In Gujarat, he said, one of the party’s MLAs had resigned, but AAP defeated the BJP in the subsequent by-election. “Wherever our elected representatives are, none of them has betrayed the people,” Kejriwal said.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Goa | Silver Rate in Goa | Bank Holidays in Goa | Public Holidays in Goa | Petrol Price in GoaStay updated with the latest Goa news. articles.title: 'Slim chance' government will hit 1.5m new homes target, Rayner tells BBC
articles.summary: High construction costs and the Iran war are threatening the key manifesto pledge, the housing secretary says.
articles.body:
There is only a "slim chance" the government will meet its target of building 1.5 million homes in England by the next election, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner has told the BBC.

"Headwinds" including the Iran war and rising construction costs are making it harder to meet the key Labour manifesto pledge, Rayner told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg.

"But I'm definitely not giving it up," she said, and stressed that the government was "making a difference" through investing billions in social and affordable homes.

Data up to March this year suggested the government was behind on the rate of construction needed to meet the goal, which housebuilders have previously warned was too optimistic.

Labour promised to hit the target through building both private and social housing by the end of the current parliament, meaning summer 2029 at the latest.

This implied an average of 300,000 new properties would be needed each year - a rate of construction not seen in decades.

Rayner told the BBC on Sunday: "It's a slim chance, but I'm definitely not giving it up."

She said it was important to keep the goal - which she said had always been a "stretch target" - in place, but that she was "being honest with the public" that it would be difficult to achieve.

"The prime minister wants us to make sure we're building council houses. He's made that absolutely, fundamentally clear," she said.

"We're seeing home starts up by 15% last year, so we are making a difference."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has promised "the biggest council house building programme since the post-war period" - although he has not provided details on exactly what this will entail.

BBC Verify analysis showed a decline in the number of new houses being built during Labour's first year in power - continuing a fall that began under the Conservatives.

Rayner's predecessor in the role, Steve Reed, last year admitted a sharp surge in construction would be needed to reach the goal - but said he expected it would just about be met once the impact of planning reforms took hold.

Analysts have said reforms introduced by Sir Keir Starmer's government should help increase construction in the long term, including changing the rules on green belt development to increase the area in which homes can be built.

But some argue that construction is being held back by factors including high house prices relative to average incomes, higher costs due to global conflict and labour shortages since Brexit.

articles.title: Longleat anniversary marked with fireworks and balloons
articles.summary: It is 60 years since the first safari park outside Africa opened its doors.
articles.body:
Hot air balloons, fireworks and aerial displays have filled the skies above Longleat to mark the safari park's 60th anniversary.

Celebrations at the Wiltshire attraction have been under way since Friday, with crowds gathering in their thousands to take in the sights.

Longleat opened six decades ago in 1966, and it has also been 50 years since the site hosted its first ever ballooning event .

Scott Ashman, head of operations at the safari park, said Saturday had been a "great second day" for the Icons of the Skies event.

As well as the hot air balloons, a number of other aerial displays including G Force Aerobatics and the RAF Falcons filled the skies above the park's stately home.

It was wonderful to welcome the RAF Falcons back for their high-intensity parachute display which was truly breathtaking," said Ashman.

"And to have the animals captured on film also watching the displays is quite incredible."

Longleat was the first safari park outside of Africa to open to the public. Today, the estate houses more than 120 species of critically endangered or vulnerable wild animals.

Sunday is the final day of celebrations marking the anniversary.
